text: The number of displayed alerts is small.
The amount of displayed alerts is appropriate.
The quality of displayed alerts is good.
Appropriate measures are taken for benign triggers.
No prior knowledge of the monitored environment is required.
The displayed information is sufficiently comprehensive.
There are no factors that cause redundant or duplicate operations.
Help and reference documentation are available and sufficiently detailed.
When an alert indicating a potential threat is displayed, the entire process from detection to escalation can be completed using only the information shown on the screen.
It is possible to explain, with valid reasoning, why an alert should be addressed or can be safely ignored.
From an interface design perspective, it is possible to distinguish between alerts that require attention and those that can be ignored.
